correctness.rationale: For all s>k>0, K>L>0, a,b>0, the exact flow primitive Ψ_H is strictly increasing and maps the nonnegative half-line onto itself. Direct speed comparison gives δ(0)>a and asymptotic δ(∞)=a, yielding exactly one critical b_c>z_0. The difference δ(z+b)-δ(z) changes sign at most once with full boundary classification, and implicit derivatives prove decreasing inlet threshold. SymPy separately verified the rational speed-ratio divided difference; the exact-flow standalone checker passed 2,331 supplementary assertions across 450 seeded parameter samples, not used as an infinite proof. value.rationale: The exact conditional length threshold and strictly moving unique inlet crossover answer a physically motivated network-arrangement question for nonlinear source-loaded uptake. They show that a source-dominated two-reach continuous system can favor the lower-affinity reach first only at low input for short downstream high-affinity residence, then reverse at a mathematically sharp inlet and lose this reversal at a uniquely defined length. This is structural information about model sequencing unavailable from the empirical half-saturation data or discrete zero-source formula alone; it is not merely a normalization or a tiny numerical gain. Model limitations and lack of field calibration are explicit.
